title: Understanding the COVID-19 Infodemic: Analyzing User-Generated Online Information During a COVID-19 Outbreak in Vietnam
screen_reason: Content analysis of Vietnamese user-generated online posts about five COVID-19 public health interventions. The 500 most-engaged posts were manually classified against external ground truth (Vietnam MoH guidelines, WHO, peer-reviewed journals) and 10/500 (2.00%) were coded misinformation. This is a quantitative share of items in a sample judged false against an external reference, i.e. CONTENT prevalence with a stated denominator.

estimates.platform: Vietnamese online platforms: social media, online forums and online newspapers (Social Media Command Center archive)
estimates.measure_type: % of the 500 most-engaged Vietnamese online posts about five COVID-19 public health interventions that were classified as misinformation
estimates.denominator: 500 online posts (the 100 posts with the highest number of engagements for each of five COVID-19 intervention topics), selected from 54,528 Vietnamese-language posts collected 1 Jul-15 Sep 2020
estimates.definition: Post 'expressed information that was easily refuted by at least one of abovementioned references' - the Official Guideline of the Vietnam Ministry of Health, official news outlets of the Vietnam government, the WHO, and/or at least two peer-reviewed scientific journals
estimates.misinfo_def: misinformation, defined in the field of public health as a 'claim of fact that is currently false due to a lack of scientific evidence'
estimates.source_quote: Among the 500 most influential posts, 316 (63.20%) contained genuine information, 10 (2.00%) contained misinformation, 152 (30.40%) were non-factual opinions, and 22 (4.40%) contained unverifiable information.
estimates.page_loc: Results, section III.2 'Descriptive and Analyzed Characteristics of Selected Online Posts', p. 312; Table 3
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two researchers independently read and categorised each of the 500 posts using the Table 1 definitions, benchmarking content against Vietnam MoH official guidelines, official Vietnamese government news outlets, the WHO and/or at least two peer-reviewed journals; the two sets were cross-checked and disputes resolved by consultation with a third researcher plus an additional information search. No kappa or other reliability statistic is reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: We selected the 100 posts with the highest number of engagements from each of the five topics, which yielded 500 posts for analysis.
estimates.notes: Headline estimate. Denominator is a rank-truncated (top-engagement) subset of a five-topic COVID-19 keyword corpus, hence denom_scope=topical with denom_selection=curated. The paper itself frames this as 'a low volume of misinformation'.

estimates.notes: Platform split of the same 500-post corpus. Both counts are verbatim (8 misinformation posts; n = 152 social media posts), so this is an exact part/whole share under R8. NOTE for adjudicator: the paper prints the column percentage (8/10 = 80% of misinformation posts came from social media), not this row percentage; 5.3% is the part/whole re-orientation, not a number printed in the paper. Confidence set to medium for that reason.

missed_or_uncertain: 1) 22/500 (4.40%) posts were 'unverified information' - information 'that could not be proven correct or incorrect by the references'. Not extracted as misinformation: by the paper's own definition these items are NOT judged false, so a wholly true item could carry the label; adding them to the 2.00% would also be a cross-category sum forbidden by R8. Flagged here because a broader-definition coder might report 32/500 (6.4%) misinformation-plus-unverified. 2) The other two platform cells are extractable on the same logic but were not written, to avoid low-value rows: online forum 2/144 (1.4%) and online newspaper 0/204 (0%) misinformation. 3) 152/500 (30.40%) were 'opinions' - non-factual opinion, not a falsity judgement, so no row. 4) Table 2 volume figures (54,528 posts; 46,035 (84.42%) during outbreak; 32,034 (58.75%) from online newspapers) are shares of posts by period/source, not by veracity, so no construct applies. 5) No survey, exposure-log, sharing or concentration data in this paper.

rob.design: Longitudinal content analysis. Frame: all publicly available Vietnamese-language online posts (social media, online forums, online newspapers with a verified Vietnamese area of operation) matching a research-team keyword list for five COVID-19 non-pharmacological interventions, 1 Jul-15 Sep 2020, drawn from the Ministry of Science and Technology's 'Social Media Command Center' internet archive (54,528 posts). Not a probability sample; classification was done only on the 100 most-engaged posts per topic (n = 500), an engagement-truncated subset. Coding procedure: two researchers independently categorised every selected post as genuine information, misinformation, opinion or unverified information using pre-specified definitions; the two sets were cross-checked and disputes resolved by a third researcher plus additional searching, with no post left unresolved. No inter-rater reliability statistic (kappa or percent agreement) is reported. Sentiment coded automatically with a Vietnamese sentiment lexicon and VnCoreNLP. Ethics approval obtained (ANU 2020/605; NIHE IRB-29/2020).
